title: I'm making a Black & White-style voxel god game with Opus 5.5
author: CapitanUncino19
selftext: The whole game is one HTML file with no asset files: every model and sound is generated in code. The trailer isn't a screen recording. A scripted camera renders it frame by frame. The music and sound effects were synthesized from a log of every sound the game played, so they line up with the picture automatically.

comments.author: Silver-Second-647
comments.body:
COOL project! I'm curious, why did you choose to synthesize all the sound effects in code instead of using audio assets? Was it mainly for easier automation or something else?

I'm exploring AI powered game audio workflows myself, so I'd love to hear your thoughts!

replies.author: CapitanUncino19
replies.body:
Thanks! Mostly speed. At this stage I want to try ideas quickly and cheaply, and generating the sounds in code was the easiest way to get audio in at all. Changing a sound is just a quick ask to the AI, and I don’t need to worry about licences etc.

I might switch to proper audio assets eventually, but I was honestly surprised how good the generated sound turned out.

replies.author: amunozo1
replies.body: It's not Pokemon Black and White, but [Black and White by Lionhead Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_%26_White_(video_game))

replies.author: CapitanUncino19
replies.body: Yes, this one! Really sad that it never got a remake.

comments.author: keytonw
comments.body: Loved Black & White. Molyneux is a genius. This looks great! Keep up the good work!

replies.author: CapitanUncino19
replies.body: It was ahead of its time!

comments.author: hyperg8_games
comments.body: rendering the trailer frame by frame with a scripted camera is a cool idea. I had Claude Code assemble my trailer too and the gameplay felt way too slow for it, how do you handle pacing with the camera? imho max 90 seconds

replies.author: CapitanUncino19
replies.body: agree on 90s, mine ended up at 45. I didn’t record gameplay at all. I described the storyboard, basically which events I wanted to see (wolf thrown into the sea, raiders getting fireballed, colossus rising...), and then the scenes were all scripted within the game, camera path included. the game gets rendered frame by frame, so each shot is only 3-4 seconds. the music and sound were generated afterwards to match the cuts
